newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: TrustPower sets buy of two NZ power firms.
newsitem.headline: TrustPower sets buy of two NZ power firms.

text.p: New Zealand electricity company TrustPower Ltd said on Friday it had sealed an outline agreement with Tauranga District Council to buy its two power companies, Tauranga Electricity Ltd and Kaimai Hydropower Ltd, for a total of NZ$38 million, payable in the form of TrustPower shares.

In a parallel statement, council holding company Tauranga Civic Holdings Ltd said it had recommended the council approve the agreement, which would lead to it owning 8.4 percent of TrustPower's equity.
TrustPower chairman Avon Carpenter said in a statement that the merger had been promoted by many in the community and the industry.

"Ours is a fiercely competitive sector and one in a process of far-reaching change. In this environment no competitor can afford inefficiency nor can any shareholder be satisfied with less than full value for energy investment," he added.
Peter Jensen of the Tauranga holding company said the recommendation had not been made lightly.

"There will be job losses. There may also be a tariff rise for TEL (Tauranga Electricity Ltd) customers as the tariffs are equalised. We recognise these issues and they are to be regretted," he added.
The anticipated gains, however, were believed to be "far to the greater good", he said.
The value of $38 million was based on TrustPower's share price, which stood at NZ$2.55, up one cent, on Friday afternoon.
Tauranga said the total represented a premium over the stand-alone values of the two companies and over their assessed maximum competitive sale value.
In addition, TrustPower has agreed to repay the district council over $14 million of loans made to the Tauranga Joint Generation Committee, as well as assuming some debt.
The deal also commits the Tauranga Energy Consumer Trust, TrustPower's biggest single shareholder, to a shareholders agreement with the proposed new council shareholder.
This could potentially mean about 5,000 further residents would become beneficiaries of the Trust after a merger and be able to participate in its returns.
